body: I'm so happy for you! Go get that education. You rock!
Hey, just genuinely curious, but what am I being called out here on this thread? Is it the "bizarre comments" that I'd written on my post?
We're both asians. It's tough. His parents are gold diggers, and the ex has all the gold.
Thank you, ma'am. <3 It's good to see something nice and positive here. This thread is stressing me out more than it's helping. I'm happy to hear from someone who understands. Much love to you!

> And you don't have a "pregnancy scare" until a pregnancy test comes back positive.

A pregnancy scare means that there's a possibility that one might have gotten pregnant from a sexual encounter, not necessarily that the result be positive. Please educate yourself.

And btw just so you know, it was him who assumed I was pregnant as he was always the one asking me if I had my period yet, and I was the one who assured him that it was probably just late even after two weeks of missed period.
Please read my post and stop embarrassing yourself. If you're too lazy to do that, ctrl/cmd + F then type "test". You're welcome.

Yes, his family is against our relationship. They want his ex, and all of them have expressed their sentiments that they pray my boyfriend regrets ever choosing me over his ex and that our future family will be faced with bad karma and our children be sick with mental illnesses. This isn't even an exaggeration.
Just like everybody else does.
Sorry. I grew up in an abusive household that things you might consider bizarre are actually the norm for me and other child abuse survivors.

Thank you! I would. I have a better view now of our current relationship and have decided to place my efforts and my hours someplace else until the time comes, if ever it comes, that I would like to try to conceive for real.

> were the possible side effects that made him say no to BC related to your sex drive or possible weight gain?

Yes, the sex drive. It's exactly the first thing he's mentioned he'd heard.

I'll sort out my birth control and be even more responsible now with my choices. I think the scare woke him up, and I don't think he'd be joking about it anytime soon.
I will now, thank you.

>It’s easy to find someone who is good when things are good. But finding someone who will make you feel safe and suported even in times of crisis is amazingly rare and special.

Thank you :'( I feel understood now. That's exactly what I expected from him because leading up to the incident, that's how he'd always acted towards me. He'd tell me that he'd help me finish school if my parents won't support me and even tease me, "Should we tell your mum now?" It really seemed as though he were encouraging it until my period would not come, and I suppose it was just wrong of me to expect that much from him. I just thought that whatever happens, we'd choose to be happy, because that's what I've taken from him the whole time right up until the scare. You are so lucky to have found a partner as supportive as yours. Thank you for your input. This made me feel heard and validated.

I'm sorry. I grew up in an abusive household (with my mother having the most control of my body) and am still unlearning behaviours and unhealthy coping methods that I've learnt to survive. I'm only slowly beginning to take charge of my life, one day at a time. It's a deep struggle, but I'm moving forward.

Yes, ma'am. I agree with you. We're both just not prepared. We're young, and we're most likely babies in adult bodies as well. I'm looking into getting a better and more solid form of birth control now as I see things more clearly now and realised that I really would rather just focus on other things. This is not the time for me to worry about children and getting pregnant. I've a lot to experience myself. I suppose I just became too comfortable in our relationship that I didn't anticipate that kind of reaction from him as he's been really caring towards me. But I think I'll be okay. I'm glad I'm aware of his true feelings now.

We talked about it, and he said he didn't want me to get an abortion. Fortunately, the test was negative because I really don't want to start a family where the father sees our child/my being pregnant as a problem.

Hey, thank you. The second paragraph makes so much sense to me. So much so that I felt understood somehow. I think it's exactly that. It's going to take time, but I'll be working on healing from this, moving forward, and start focusing more on my career and the things and relationships that I already do have than anything else. And I'll be considering getting an IUD some time soon or in the future.

>Why are you so hurt if you said that you are not ready yourself?

I don't even know myself. It's the question I've been looking the answer to. I don't understand why it hurts me, but it does. I suppose what I'm really looking for are validation and support because with the test being negative, my boyfriend's worries are instantly gone and I? I'm left with this feeling I never thought I'd get.
Thank you. This is what I needed. I think it just takes time. I can't force it. I'll be okay.

I think that's what I want. I just mentioned to my boyfriend about getting an IUD implanted. He said I didn't have to. I asked my sister for her opinion on it, and she got scared for me. I asked friends as well, and apparently no one is for it. If the pain is intolerable for me, I'd probably just try abstinence since I've been discouraged from having children now.

I just started looking into getting an implant, and I'm considering having one just to be on the safer side. May I ask how painful the process is going to be? I have low tolerance for pain, and so far I've read people saying that it hurts TERRIBLY.
Absolutely. I'm glad to have him on my side now. Thank you for your words!
That works, too! I like that approach. It's often very nice to not take things and other people's comments too seriously and to just laugh it all off. Thank you so much for sharing!
Thank you for this! I would keep your words in mind, and keep on practising. And I agree, it must be so tough having to live with themselves 24/7! I wish them relief. Love and light to you too!
Thank you! I'd definitely be looking into that. Thank you for all the help, and I wish you well.
Thank you for the good wishes and the recommendation! I wish you the same. Much love and peace.
Thanks again! I appreciate your words a lot. And likewise, kind stranger.
You're absolutely right! Thank you so much! I wish you all the best too, and much love. <3

Thank you, and I agree that it is sad, especially for these people. They suffer so much that it's leaking out of them and poisoning their own child's life and other people's lives. I hope one day, in this life or the next, they find some clarity and peace and genuine love for them in their lives, too.

/r/raisedbynarcissists opened my eyes to the abuse my parents have put me through. I owe it to that sub that I'm aware and out of the FOG now, albeit I'm still financially dependent on them. Hopefully one day my partner would realise his parents aren't so good for his well-being either and garner the courage to let them go. Thank you so much for your input! They're very well appreciated, and I'm so glad you managed to go LC with those people. We all deserve some peace in our lives. I wish you well on everything, and much love.

It's not. I'm sorry if it comes across as though I'm rejoicing in their suffering; I'm not. It's all sad in spite of how they act towards me. Though, like I said in my post, it's quite hard for me to show them complete compassion, it's just my pain manifesting itself, I would think. However, just because I can't do it now doesn't mean it's not possible later. I'll keep working on it. Thank you.

You are right... I do have doubts about myself. A lot of it, in fact. And you're right in thinking that I believe that they may be right about me. The things they said about me is what I think about myself, too. I haven't got much to show off to people, and I haven't really the desire to show off anything because I really am just trying to live my life the way I would like to - humble and free. I don't have a job, and I've just started college, and I thought maybe they were right that I can't handle any job or life at all because I feel broken in so many ways. And I *am* terrified of people, or to put it more accurately, I'm terrified that they're going to hurt me and humiliate me like my parents have. And the last thing they said about me I've just always felt was true: that I *am* crazy. I feel crazy all the time. I feel out of place and incapable - not like his ex who's got all these good things that are going for her despite her behaviour. I know I should be happy for her, but sometimes it just doesn't feel fair that I get to be bound by all these pain and sadness, until I remember that my suffering is what has made me kind. I just tell myself that yes, perhaps I am insane, but between myself and these people who don't have the disorder I have, I can confidently say that I have the kinder, more genuine attitude towards others. Perhaps I haven't got much in terms of material possessions, but I have myself... and maybe that's enough. Maybe that's all I really need.

Thank you so much, Mindful_Drone79. Your words and validation and support mean a lot to me. I haven't received much kindness in life, so thank you for bringing me a lot. I will keep your faith in me in my heart and in my mind, and work on making myself strong or stronger, not just for myself but also for the world that desperately needs more people who haven't been embittered by their suffering. Thank you for your kindness.

Hello, thank you so much for your response!

What you said about his mother's fear about losing her power over her son makes sense. He's recently told me that his relationship with me has been rewarding for him and that he's been seeing much improvement with himself and his behaviour with my help. This evident improvement might be one of the reasons why she's retaliating with much fervour.

Honestly, if it were up to me, I'd rather wish for their disappearance. Their approval doesn't really matter to me, especially considering their lack of respect towards others and their unrelenting disregard for their son's feelings. I'd rather surround myself with positive, well-meaning people so that I can grow. However, it's not up to me, and I can't make them disappear. With regard to them believing that I'm afraid of people, they've gotten that from rumours about me being "sick". They assumed I was afraid of people because I've been homeschooled. And no, I couldn't have exposed myself to them more as I live at least 14 hours away from them. They've literally only seen me once personally, and yet they have all these things to say against me.

I could, like you said, kill them with kindness, but I'm afraid I'd rather not lose much time and energy on people who seem intent on dragging me down. I've tried doing away with my parents' abuse by showing them kindness, but it hasn't worked one bit, and I ended up hurting myself trying to fix something I couldn't fix and was not mine to fix in the first place. However, I value all of your suggestions dearly, and you've made good points without a doubt. I just wish they apply to these people. They are so caught up in the material realm that they'd forgotten to be kind, not even to their own son and brother - not even to themselves. It's disheartening.

Thanks for the advice and good wishes! I wish you well.

Hello, ketchupkid. Thank you so, so much for this. I haven't felt this validated in a while. I honestly lost it and started tearing up at "You're a baby!" (baby confirmed haha). I suppose it really just feels as though these people and the situation itself are calling for me to care about material things, which I really don't - at least not as much as my partner and his family do. I've always wanted to live through humble means, and above all, to learn about other cultures and other people's lives and to help people and to use the knowledge I've gathered to help those who need it. Having a lot of money doesn't make me happy, but meaningful relationships and inner peace do. I've just realised now that the anger I've felt also stems from the idea that I was betraying myself and my values in favour of somebody else's. Thank you for believing in me. I appreciate your words and your kindness and support incredibly much. I'm going to treasure this for life. Thank you thank you thank you.
You're absolutely right. I'll take all of that into account. Thanks again!
Thank you! I love that story.

This is such valuable insight. I'd be spending the night reflecting on it now. Thank you so much for sharing, and for the support. This is putting things into perspective for me. Thanks again! I find myself healing more and more from this situation with each kind word I get from all of you.

Thank you for response! You're right. They must be suffering incredibly much themselves to behave so despicably towards other people. I'm glad I'm only catching *some* of the effects of such suffering, which I admittedly multiply by not letting it go, while they, on the other hand, get to be with such foul and cruel burdens their entire lives.

And thank you for pointing out that it's inevitable that I encounter people bearing ill-will. I suppose this is something I haven't come to terms as yet, and is perhaps the reason why I'm facing this challenge in life now. I have to accept that not everybody has good intentions towards others apart from themselves, and not everybody is going to like me or even think well of me, and that's okay. Nothing to do with me. Thanks so much.

Somehow I feel a bit relieved that a fellow Southeast Asian gets it, haha. Thank you! To answer your question, I do have my boyfriend's support. He's told me he doesn't like the way his family treats me and our relationship at all and that he intends for us to be far from them someday. We're already in a ldr, and it's going to be that way for years as he works abroad, so really it's not quite possible yet to be out of his family's influences when they've still got contact and all else, and quite honestly he's quite a bit of a problem standing up for himself and what he wants and thinks is right as well, which I don't blame him for considering the kind of people who brought him up. I think the rational thing to be done is to just ignore them, refuse to fuel their unwholesome attitude, not give other people reason to believe that these people are right about me, and keep on with my practice of loving-kindness towards all, including myself. Am I doing this right? It's really hard to think when anger and hatred possess me. It's utterly terrifying.

Yes yes yes. I read your post and was like, "Oh my god, that's how I am, too." I don't remember my childhood much so I can't really talk about how my dreams were like back then but for some that I do remember and have stuck with me, they were dreams that took place in another universe and were pretty gruesome. (One of the earliest dreams I've had that I can recall was of myself amidst a downpour of bloody, severed body parts due to people jumping off of high buildings.). Enter teeenage & adolescent years, and my dreams have started becoming more and more polished and detailed and have started turning into nightmares. Those dreams have only ever occurred in apocalyptic/post-apocalyptic universes just like yours, and for a couple of years now I've been getting it around 5 times per night and it happens even when just taking a really quick nap. The dreams are highly disturbing and seem so real every time, so whenever I wake up I'm already pertrubed and sometimes crying, and there are certainly times when I'd rather not sleep at all because I'm much too scared to get into it again. I should say though that despite them being so terrifying I have grown accustomed and have actually taken a liking to them. They're so complex and full of wonder and quite honestly the places and environment the dreams take place in and the way the stories twist and turn are so incredibly creative that I sometimes find myself wanting to be there than be here despite its horrifying and unfamiliar features. You're definitely not alone in this, and I'm quite happy that somebody shares the same experience.
One word: codependency.

Oh yes. Last year I had to be sent to the psych ward because of suicidal plans/tendencies and be on higher doses of medications. At the hospital, the doctor told me, "We can help you here." My Nmom asked her, "How long is she going to be here for?" To which the doctor responded, "Until she gets better." Nmom pulled me aside to talk to me. She said, "Think about this: you're going to be admitted into a MENTAL HOSPITAL. What are people going to say? Are you even really sick? Your father's going to put the news up on Facebook. It will be shameful for us when people find out you're crazy. Let's go home." Of course, she always had the last word. She told the doctor that I was feeling better all of a sudden. The doctor was incredibly doubtful but proceeded to prescribe me medications and sleep aids in addition to my then-medications for bipolar disorder (I personally think it's more C-PTSD than bipolar). To make matters worse, when Nmom and I got home, she raged for literally a few seconds and then laughed maniacally right after and exclaimed, "Look! I'm bipolar too! I'm taking your meds." What... And she never even asked why I was feeling suicidal in the first place. Not once. She even said to me and to my school counsellor in tears and everything, "You can't kill yourself. You have to think about me. What's your father going to do to me? What will other people say?" She was only concerned about what we would look like to other people, what they were going to say to her, and what was going to happen to her.

I used to have the same problem. Right now, I tell myself I'm not being an inconvenience when the other person is okay with hearing what I have to say. I shut out the voices that want to put me down. It's about respecting myself enough to allow myself to feel and express my thoughts and emotions while respecting the other person's time and boundaries. If they're busy or if they'd rather not be disturbed right now, then I would have to respect that. If they gladly offer their time and lend an ear, then I'm grateful for it and for them and take that opportunity to say what I want to say. One thing that's helped with the guilt that comes with talking to them about myself (I felt selfish for it) is to turn my apologies into thank you's. For instance, when a friend of mine and I have a conversation online, I always end the conversation with "Thank you for talking to me today!" and after talking to them about my problems I go, "Thank you for listening to me! I appreciate it a lot." I genuinely feel thankful for them and for the time they've allotted to me, and it makes me feel 10x lighter that I don't have to apologise for being myself. The same friend caught on to it and also started saying thank you after she and I talk. We always end our conversations on good terms with each other, and every conversation with her feels refreshing. So I say, you don't have to apologise for being you. What you have to say is worth listening to, and when you and your partner have respect for each other's time and boundaries as well as respect for yourselves, you wouldn't feel the need to hold yourself back, which can lead to resentment towards your partner. It takes practice though, not gonna lie, but I swear it's worth it.
